body:
You need to use `PROPERTY_USAGE_ALWAYS_DUPLICATE` to force the duplication of nested items.

```gdscript
@export_custom(PROPERTY_HINT_NONE, "", PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE & PROPERTY_USAGE_ALWAYS_DUPLICATE) var _corners: PackedVector2Array
```

Oh. I can't say I knew that usage flag even existed, but that's definitely good to know. Thank you very much for informing me.

I still stand by my previous sentiment though, in that I don't think this is really expected behavior from most people when making a "Unique" duplication of a `@tool` resource. The odd mutations this behavior caused forced me to research its cause for a frustrating amount of time, being completely puzzled as to why one resource's behavior was inexplicably imitating another's. I fear that other tool devs will fall into this very specific bug-search trap in the future, causing an unneeded waste of time all around.

I really don't think using `duplicate_deep(RESOURCE_DEEP_DUPLICATE_NONE)` would add a significant amount of editor overhead to get around this issue, but feel free to correct me if I'm wrong.

If it's still deemed that the editor functionality _shouldn't_ be changed, then I'd at least try to emphasize this particular scenario better to the user. Like, adding a warning if using `@export_storage` on an array with a `@tool` resource, as that would almost certainly be a use case where one would also want to use `PROPERTY_USAGE_ALWAYS_DUPLICATE`. I'd even suggest simply having `@export_storage` apply that usage flag automatically when used on arrays, though I _do_ fear that doing so would cause some kind of regression in someone's obscure resource setup.

Okay, I've tested out your usage flag suggestion.

Firstly, you used the wrong bitwise operator, as there's supposed to be a `|` instead of `&`. Combining the flags with `&` resulted in the `_corners` array not being saved into the resource at all. This initially gave me the impression of it working, but that was just a side-effect of how non-storage elements don't get copied in the duplication process at all.

Secondly... it surprisingly just doesn't work! Despite being given `PROPERTY_USAGE_ALWAYS_DUPLICATE`, the `_corners` array simply just doesn't duplicate, which I think is an entirely new bug in its own right.

Yeah, looking into the source code for the resource class, it seems that `PROPERTY_USAGE_ALWAYS_DUPLICATE` is only mentioned once, and the way it's used _only_ accounts for objects. 
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/57277407e77e61b161f35dbd7aeb510f7a9e26a6/core/io/resource.cpp#L278-L290

This seems like a bit of an oversight, as the [official documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_@globalscope.html#enum-globalscope-propertyusageflags) make no mention of this behavior only applying to objects.
> ### [PropertyUsageFlags](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_@globalscope.html#enum-globalscope-propertyusageflags) **PROPERTY_USAGE_ALWAYS_DUPLICATE** = `524288`
> When duplicating a resource with [Resource.duplicate()](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_resource.html#class-resource-method-duplicate), and this flag is set on a property of that resource, the property should always be duplicated, regardless of the `subresources` bool parameter.
